specs.title: CSV export of reports
sources: Owner request: 'Add CSV export to the reports page, and a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports' (export part)
Current behaviour of the reports page
in_scope: A user on the reports page can download the report they are viewing as a CSV file
non_goals: The partner REST API (separate line and spec: 'Partner reports API')
Other export formats (Excel, PDF)
Scheduled or emailed exports
Changes to the reports page table itself

criteria.text: Given a user viewing a report on the reports page, when they choose Export CSV, then a CSV file downloads whose header row lists the report's visible columns in the order shown on the page.
criteria.check: Integration/UI test: trigger export, parse the file, compare header to the page's columns.

criteria.text: Given a report with filters applied, when the user exports, then the rows in the file are those defined by open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with a filtered report comparing file rows to the expected set (written once Q1 is answered).

criteria.text: Given a report with no rows, when the user exports, then the result is as defined by open question 2.
criteria.check: Negative test on an empty report (written once Q2 is answered).

criteria.text: Given a user without access to the reports page, when they request an export directly, then the export is refused and no data is returned.
criteria.check: Negative integration test: unauthenticated and unauthorized requests receive a refusal and an empty body.

expected_areas: Reports data access used by the page

open_questions.question: Does the export follow the filters the user has applied, or export the whole report?

options.option: Follow the applied filters
options.changes: File matches what the user sees; criterion 2 tests filtered rows

options.option: Always the whole report
options.changes: Filters are ignored; criterion 2 tests the full row set

open_questions.question: What happens when the report has no rows?

options.option: Download a file with the header row only
options.changes: Criterion 3 checks a header-only file

options.option: Disable export and show a message
options.changes: Criterion 3 checks the disabled control and the message

specs.title: Partner reports API
sources: Owner request: 'Add CSV export to the reports page, and a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports' (API part)
in_scope: Partners outside the organisation can fetch the same reports through a public REST API
non_goals: CSV export on the reports page (separate line and spec: 'CSV export of reports')
Writing or changing report data through the API
A partner self-service portal or onboarding flow

criteria.text: Given a partner with valid credentials and access to a report, when they request that report from the API, then the response contains the same rows and columns the reports page shows for that report.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the API response with the page's data for the same report and parameters.

criteria.text: Given a request with missing or invalid credentials, when it reaches the API, then it is refused with an authentication error and no report data.
criteria.check: Negative integration test: no credentials, expired credentials, malformed credentials.

criteria.text: Given a partner with valid credentials, when they request a report they are not entitled to, then the request is refused and no data from that report is returned.
criteria.check: Negative integration test: partner A requests a report only partner B may see (isolation).

criteria.text: Given a partner exceeding the request limit set by open question 3, when they send another request, then it is refused with a rate-limit error until the window passes.
criteria.check: Integration test with a mocked clock (written once Q3 is answered).

open_questions.question: How do partners authenticate, and who issues and revokes their credentials?

options.option: API keys issued by an admin
options.changes: Simple to build; criterion 2 tests key checks; revocation is manual

options.option: OAuth client credentials
options.changes: More work; standard rotation and scopes

open_questions.question: Which reports and which data may each partner see? Do the reports contain personal data that may not leave the system?

options.option: Each partner sees only reports about its own business
options.changes: Criterion 3 tests per-partner isolation

options.option: All partners see the same set of reports
options.changes: Criterion 3 tests only the excluded reports

open_questions.question: What request limit applies to partners?

options.option: A fixed limit per partner (owner names the number)
options.changes: Criterion 4 tests that number

options.option: No limit in this version
options.changes: Criterion 4 is removed

actions_now: Write two separate draft specs, one per line and branch, and send the owner the open questions. The API's authentication, data exposure and isolation questions are security and privacy decisions, so I escalate them. The API line waits on them; the CSV line can start on criteria 1 and 4.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: Owner request: 'Add dark mode to the settings page, as a toggle that applies to the whole app'
Current app: settings page, in-app screens, email templates, printable invoice view
in_scope: A dark mode toggle on the settings page
When on, the app's screens use a dark appearance
non_goals: New themes beyond light and dark
Redesign of any screen beyond its colours
Email templates and the printable invoice view unless open question 1 includes them

criteria.text: Given a user on the settings page, when they switch the dark mode toggle on, then every in-app screen shows the dark appearance without a page reload.
criteria.check: UI test: toggle on, visit each top-level screen, assert dark theme applied; manual visual pass.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user switches the toggle off, then every in-app screen returns to the light appearance.
criteria.check: UI test: toggle off, revisit screens, assert light theme.

criteria.text: Given the user has chosen a mode, when they leave and come back to the app, then the mode they chose is still applied.
criteria.check: UI test: set mode, reload / new session, assert mode retained (scope of 'come back' per open question 2).

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when any in-app screen is shown, then text and controls meet the project's contrast requirement.
criteria.check: Automated contrast check (e.g. accessibility lint) on each top-level screen in dark mode.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when an email is sent or an invoice is printed, then their appearance is as defined by open question 1.
criteria.check: Manual step on a sent test email and a print preview of an invoice (written once Q1 is answered).

open_questions.question: Does 'the whole app' include the email templates and the printable invoice view?

options.option: No, in-app screens only
options.changes: Emails and print stay light; criterion 5 checks they are unchanged

options.option: Yes, include them
options.changes: Large extra work: email client support, print readability; criterion 5 checks dark versions

open_questions.question: Does the choice persist only on this device or across the user's devices, and what is the default for a user who never chose?

options.option: Per device, default light
options.changes: No server storage; criterion 3 tests same device only

options.option: Per account, default follows the system setting
options.changes: Needs stored preference; criterion 3 tests a second device

actions_now: Write the dark mode spec as a draft. Whether 'whole app' covers the email templates and the printable invoice is an open question for the owner, not something I decide. Criteria 1, 2 and 4 can go ahead now.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: The existing draft spec 'Dark mode' (content unchanged)
Provisional approval by the coordinating session, recorded in the decision queue as waiting for the owner
non_goals: Unchanged from the draft

criteria.text: All numbered criteria unchanged from the complete draft.
criteria.check: Each criterion keeps its existing check.

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): approved-provisional by the coordinating session while the owner is away; decision queue entry waits for the owner's approval; not approved by the owner.

actions_now: Pass the complete draft to the coordinating session, which the binding allows to approve it provisionally. The product role does not approve its own spec. The spec header becomes approved-provisional, names the coordinating session and the decision-queue id, and marks the approval as waiting for the owner, so work built on it carries provisional: true and is reported as provisional, not verified.

specs.title: Complete report exports for finance reconciliation
sources: Owner request: 'Exports must contain every column of the report, so finance can reconcile'
Decision dl-009: 'Personal emails never leave the system in any export'
Current report columns, including Customer email
in_scope: Report exports contain every column of the report, subject to the conflict with dl-009 being resolved
non_goals: Changing dl-009 or any other privacy decision
Changing which columns the report itself shows
New export formats

criteria.text: Given a report, when it is exported, then the export contains every column of the report except Customer email, in the report's order.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the export's header to the report's column list.

criteria.text: Given a report row, when it is exported, then each exported value equals the value shown in the report for that row and column.
criteria.check: Integration test on a seeded report comparing values cell by cell.

criteria.text: Given a report with a Customer email column, when it is exported, then the Customer email column is handled as defined by open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test on the exported file (written once Q1 is answered).

open_questions.question: The request says every column; dl-009 says personal emails never leave the system in any export. Which applies to the Customer email column?

options.option: Keep dl-009: export omits Customer email
options.changes: Export is complete except email; finance reconciles without it

options.option: Keep dl-009, replace email with a non-personal key (e.g. customer id)
options.changes: Finance gets a reconciliation key without personal data; criterion 3 tests the replacement

options.option: Owner revises dl-009 for this export
options.changes: Email leaves the system; needs a new recorded decision and a privacy review

actions_now: Write a draft spec and escalate the conflict to the owner. The request contradicts dl-009, and the question is a privacy decision. I don't pick an answer or quietly drop the column; criteria 1 and 2 can go ahead while criterion 3 waits.

No spec is needed. The request already states testable, numbered acceptance criteria with checks, and the product-spec skill doesn't cover that. I tell the factory to send the request straight to the next role, and note that it touches authentication, so verification's security negative tests apply.

specs.title: CSV export of reports
sources: Owner request: 'Let users export reports as CSV'
Current reports page: table with Date, Region, Orders, Revenue; date-range filter; current access rules for the page
in_scope: A user on the reports page can download the report table as a CSV file
non_goals: Other formats (Excel, PDF)
Scheduled or emailed exports
New columns or filters on the reports page
An API for exports

criteria.text: Given a user on the reports page, when they choose Export CSV, then a CSV file downloads with a header row Date, Region, Orders, Revenue in that order.
criteria.check: Integration/UI test: trigger export, parse file, assert header.

criteria.text: Given the table shows a set of rows, when the user exports, then each data row in the file has the same Date, Region, Orders and Revenue values as the corresponding table row.
criteria.check: Integration test on seeded data comparing file rows to table rows.

criteria.text: Given a date-range filter is applied, when the user exports, then the rows in the file are those defined by open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with a filtered table (written once Q1 is answered).

criteria.text: Given the table has no rows (for example the filter matches nothing), when the user exports, then the result is as defined by open question 2.
criteria.check: Negative test on an empty table (written once Q2 is answered).

criteria.text: Given a user who has no access to the reports page, when they request the export directly, then the request is refused and no report data is returned.
criteria.check: Negative integration test: unauthenticated and unauthorized requests get a refusal and no data.

open_questions.question: Does the export follow the applied date-range filter or always export the whole report?

options.option: Follow the filter
options.changes: File matches the screen; criterion 3 tests filtered rows

options.option: Whole report
options.changes: Filter ignored; criterion 3 tests full rows

open_questions.question: What happens when there are no rows to export?

options.option: Header-only file
options.changes: Criterion 4 checks a file with the header row only

options.option: Export disabled with a message
options.changes: Criterion 4 checks the disabled control and message text

open_questions.question: How are dates and Revenue written (date format, currency symbol, decimal separator, encoding)?

options.option: Machine-readable: ISO dates, plain numbers, UTF-8
options.changes: Easy to import into spreadsheets and tools; criterion 2 compares raw values

options.option: As displayed on the page
options.changes: Matches the screen; criterion 2 compares formatted strings

actions_now: Write the draft spec from the template, with numbered criteria, their checks and failure paths. I send the owner the open questions on filter, empty state and value format. Criteria 1 and 5 can go ahead now.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec 'CSV export' version 2, approved (dl-015)
QA report: the spec is silent on exports over 100,000 rows; the current code times out
in_scope: Behaviour when an export would exceed 100,000 rows
non_goals: Changes to version 2's other criteria
General performance work on the reports page

criteria.text: Criteria of version 2 unchanged.
criteria.check: Their existing checks.

criteria.text: Given an export that would contain more than 100,000 rows, when the user requests it, then the outcome is as defined by open question 1 and the request never ends in a timeout.
criteria.check: Integration test with a seeded data set above 100,000 rows (exact assertion written once Q1 is answered).

open_questions.question: What should happen when an export would exceed 100,000 rows?

options.option: Refuse with a message asking the user to narrow the filter
options.changes: Smallest change; large exports are not possible

options.option: Generate in the background and notify the user when the file is ready
options.changes: All data exportable; more work (jobs, notification, file storage)

options.option: Split into several files of at most 100,000 rows
options.changes: All data exportable synchronously; the user handles several files

versions: 3 (2026-11-27): draft; adds behaviour above 100,000 rows after QA's report; waits for the owner's answer and approval.

actions_now: Ask the owner in chat what should happen above 100,000 rows, giving the options and what each changes. I open draft version 3 for the answer and don't edit approved version 2. Once the owner answers and approves, version 3 replaces version 2, and what was built is checked against it.

specs.title: Dashboard performance
sources: Owner request: 'Make the dashboard faster'
Current dashboard: views Overview, Sales, Inventory
in_scope: Load time of the dashboard views named by open question 1
non_goals: New dashboard features or views
Changes to what the views show
Performance of pages other than the dashboard

criteria.text: Given the current dashboard, when each view is loaded under the measurement conditions of open question 2, then its baseline load time is recorded.
criteria.check: Command: a repeatable performance measurement run per view; output saved as the baseline.

criteria.text: Given the change is built, when each in-scope view is loaded under the same conditions, then its load time meets the target set by open question 3.
criteria.check: The same measurement command, compared against the target.

criteria.text: Given the change is built, when each view is loaded, then it shows the same data as before the change.
criteria.check: Existing view tests plus a comparison of rendered data before and after.

open_questions.question: Which views must be faster: Overview, Sales, Inventory, or all three?

options.option: All three
options.changes: Widest scope

options.option: Only the views users complain about
options.changes: Owner names them; smaller scope

open_questions.question: What is measured, and where: first load or every load, which percentile, which data size and environment?

options.option: p95 time to fully rendered view, production-like data
options.changes: Reflects what most users see

options.option: Median time on a reference machine
options.changes: Easier to measure, less representative

open_questions.question: How fast is fast enough?

options.option: An absolute target (owner names the seconds)
options.changes: Criterion 2 checks against that number

options.option: A relative improvement over the baseline (owner names the percentage)
options.changes: Criterion 2 compares to criterion 1's baseline

actions_now: Escalate to the owner, because the goal itself is unclear: which views, what is measured, and how fast is enough. I write a draft spec whose target criterion waits on those answers, and I invent no numbers. Measuring the baseline once the measurement conditions are agreed is the only part that can go ahead.

specs.title: Checkout discount
sources: Owner request: 'Add a discount to checkout'
Binding: no provisional choices for prices
in_scope: A discount applied to the order total at checkout, as defined by the owner's answers
non_goals: Changes to base prices
Other promotions or loyalty programmes
Changes to payment processing

criteria.text: Given an eligible customer (per open question 2), when they reach checkout, then the discount (per open question 1) is shown and deducted from the total they pay.
criteria.check: Integration test on checkout totals (written once Q1 and Q2 are answered).

criteria.text: Given a customer who is not eligible, when they reach checkout, then no discount is applied and the total is unchanged.
criteria.check: Negative integration test (written once Q2 is answered).

criteria.text: Given an order that also qualifies for another offer, when the customer checks out, then the offers combine as defined by open question 3.
criteria.check: Integration test with two qualifying offers (written once Q3 is answered).

criteria.text: Given a discount larger than the order total, when the customer checks out, then the total never goes below zero.
criteria.check: Negative test with a small order (limit case).

open_questions.question: How large is the discount?

options.option: A percentage of the order (owner names it)
options.changes: Scales with order size

options.option: A fixed amount (owner names it and the currency)
options.changes: Needs a minimum order or the total-floor rule

open_questions.waiting_for: owner (price decision; no provisional choice allowed)

open_questions.question: Who gets it, and how: everyone, first orders, customers with a code, a customer group?

options.option: Everyone automatically
options.changes: No eligibility check

options.option: With a discount code
options.changes: Adds code entry and invalid/expired-code failure paths

options.option: A named customer group
options.changes: Needs an eligibility rule

open_questions.question: Does it combine with other offers?

options.option: Combines
options.changes: Both deducted; criterion 3 checks the order of application

options.option: Does not combine; the larger applies
options.changes: Criterion 3 checks only one is applied

actions_now: Write a draft spec and escalate the amount, eligibility and stacking questions to the owner. They are money decisions, and the binding forbids provisional price choices. Implementation of the discount waits; I invent no values.

Put the spec in front of the owner in chat as an approval request: the spec, its sources and any known weaknesses. It stays draft until the owner approves it, and the implementer doesn't start on it until then. I don't approve it myself; once the owner answers, the approval is recorded from the owner's own words with a decision-log id.

No spec is needed. This is a bug fix with a known cause, and the expected behaviour is already defined by the page's current behaviour minus the image. I return it to the factory to go straight to the implementer, with a regression test for a user without an avatar.

specs.title: Theme and language follow the user across devices
sources: Owner request: 'Add a user_preferences table with theme and language columns, so users keep their settings across devices'
in_scope: A signed-in user's theme and language settings are the same on every device they sign in on
non_goals: Other settings beyond theme and language
Settings for signed-out visitors
New themes or languages
How the settings are stored (a table is the architect's decision; the request's user_preferences table is passed on as a suggestion)

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user who sets the theme on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B shows the theme they chose.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions of the same user.

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user who sets the language on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B shows the language they chose.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions of the same user.

criteria.text: Given a user who has never set a theme or language, when they sign in, then they see the defaults defined by open question 2.
criteria.check: Test with a new user account (written once Q2 is answered).

criteria.text: Given two users, when one changes their settings, then the other user's settings do not change.
criteria.check: Negative integration test with two accounts.

criteria.text: Given a setting change that cannot be saved, when the user changes it, then the outcome is as defined by open question 3.
criteria.check: Negative test with the save failing (written once Q3 is answered).

open_questions.question: Is the user_preferences table a requirement (for example for another system that reads it) or a suggestion of how to build it?

options.option: Suggestion
options.changes: The architect chooses the storage; the spec checks behaviour only

options.option: Requirement
options.changes: Becomes a recorded constraint for the architect, with its reason

open_questions.question: What does a user see before choosing, and what happens to settings already chosen on a device before this change?

options.option: Defaults are light theme and the browser language; existing device choices are uploaded on first sign-in
options.changes: No user loses a setting

options.option: Defaults only; existing device choices are discarded
options.changes: Simpler; some users see their settings reset once

open_questions.question: When two devices change a setting at the same time, or saving fails, what should the user see?

options.option: The latest change wins; a failed save shows an error and keeps the previous value
options.changes: Criterion 5 checks the error and the unchanged value

options.option: Keep the change locally and retry later
options.changes: Criterion 5 checks the retry

actions_now: Write the spec as behaviour, settings following the user across devices, and keep the requested table out of it as design. I pass the table to the architect as a suggestion and ask the owner whether it is a hard requirement, along with the defaults and failure questions. Criteria 1, 2 and 4 can go ahead.

specs.title: Colleagues' last-online time
sources: Team lead's request, passed on by the owner without comment: 'Show each user when their colleagues were last online'
in_scope: Showing a user the last-online time of their colleagues, within the limits the owner sets
non_goals: Live presence or activity tracking beyond last-online time
Reports or exports of users' online history
Managers' monitoring dashboards

criteria.text: Given a user permitted to see a colleague's status (per open question 1), when they view that colleague, then they see the colleague's last-online time.
criteria.check: Integration test with two users in the permitted relation (written once Q1 is answered).

criteria.text: Given a user not permitted to see a colleague's status, when they view that colleague or call the underlying data directly, then no last-online time is returned.
criteria.check: Negative integration test, including a direct request (written once Q1 is answered).

criteria.text: Given a user who has hidden their status (if open question 2 allows it), when a colleague views them, then no last-online time is shown.
criteria.check: Negative test (written once Q2 is answered).

criteria.text: Given last-online data older than the retention period of open question 3, when the retention job runs, then that data no longer exists.
criteria.check: Test with a mocked clock (written once Q3 is answered).

open_questions.question: Who may see a user's last-online time?

options.option: Members of the same team
options.changes: Narrow exposure; needs a team relation

options.option: Everyone in the organisation
options.changes: Wider exposure of personal data

options.option: Managers only
options.changes: Becomes monitoring of employees; higher privacy and people-related risk

open_questions.question: Can users hide their last-online time?

options.option: Yes, opt-out
options.changes: Adds a setting; criterion 3 applies

options.option: Yes, opt-in (hidden by default)
options.changes: Privacy-preserving default; criterion 3 tests the default

options.option: No
options.changes: Criterion 3 removed; may need a legal basis

open_questions.question: How long is last-online data kept, and is only the latest time kept or a history?

options.option: Only the latest time, overwritten
options.changes: Minimal data; criterion 4 checks no history exists

options.option: History for a period the owner names
options.changes: More data held; criterion 4 checks deletion after that period

actions_now: Write a draft spec and escalate to the owner, not the team lead. Who may see the time, whether users can hide it, and how long it is kept are privacy and people decisions that I don't answer. All criteria wait on those answers, so no build work starts.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec 'CSV export' version 1, approved (dl-014)
Implementer's report: criterion 3 requires customer emails, the reports API returns none, and adding them is outside this line
in_scope: Everything in version 1 except criterion 3, which is open
non_goals: Changes to the reports API within this line, unless the owner chooses to widen it or open a new line

criteria.text: Criteria 1, 2 and 4 onward of version 1 unchanged.
criteria.check: Their existing checks.

criteria.text: Given an export, when it is generated, then the customer's email is handled as defined by open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test on the exported file (written once Q1 is answered).

open_questions.question: Criterion 3 asks for the customer's email, which the reports API does not provide. What should change?

options.option: Drop the email from the export in this version
options.changes: This line finishes without API changes; finance or users lose the email column

options.option: Keep the email; open a separate line to add emails to the reports API first
options.changes: Export waits on that line; personal emails leave the system, which needs a privacy decision

options.option: Widen this line to include the API change
options.changes: Larger line; same privacy decision needed

versions: 2 (2026-11-27): draft; criterion 3 reopened after the implementer's report; waits for the owner's answer and approval.

actions_now: Don't edit approved version 1 and don't tell the implementer by message to skip criterion 3. I open draft version 2 with criterion 3 as an open question and ask the owner to choose: drop the email, or add it through a separate or widened line (a privacy decision). The other criteria can proceed; criterion 3 waits.
